topic_title: Top 15 Best Small Dog Breeds Under 25 Pounds
intro: Being small does not make a dog easy. Some toy and terrier breeds bark at every sound, chase cats or are too fragile for a busy household, while others are calm, quick to train and relaxed with visitors. Before choosing, look at three things: how much the breed barks, how well it gets along with children and other animals, and the coat care it needs, because several of the smallest dogs need daily brushing or regular trips to a groomer. Energy matters too, since a few small terriers need more exercise than many large dogs.

picks.description: The Cavalier is the most even-tempered dog on this list. At 13 to 18 pounds it is sturdy enough for family life, it gets along with children, cats and other dogs, and it is rated low for barking, which makes it easy to live with in a house or a flat. Around 30 to 45 minutes of walks and play a day is enough, and it is easy to train with gentle, reward-based methods. The silky, medium-length coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a few times a week, with extra attention to the feathered ears. The main trade-offs are health and company: the breed is prone to heart and neurological conditions, its lifespan is 9 to 14 years, and it dislikes being left alone for long stretches.
picks.best_for: Families or retirees home most of the day wanting a gentle dog
picks.quirky_fact: Cavaliers are named after King Charles II of England, who was rarely seen without his small spaniels.
picks.skip_if: You are out for long workdays or cannot budget for possible heart care

picks.description: The Havanese is a cheerful, sturdy small dog of 7 to 13 pounds that is easy to train and friendly with children, cats and other dogs. Its energy is moderate: two walks and some indoor play a day keep it content, and it enjoys learning tricks. The long, silky coat sheds little but tangles if neglected, so plan on brushing several times a week, or keep it in a short clip with a professional trim every six to eight weeks. Havanese will bark to announce visitors but are not usually persistent barkers. They are strongly attached to their people and can develop separation anxiety if left alone for many hours, so they suit households where someone is home for much of the day. A 14 to 16 year lifespan is a long commitment.
picks.best_for: Households home often who want a happy, low-shedding small dog
picks.quirky_fact: The Havanese is the national dog of Cuba and was kept by Cuban aristocratic families in the 1800s.
picks.skip_if: The dog would be alone most of the day or coat care sounds tiresome

picks.description: The Boston Terrier gives you a small dog with very little grooming. Its short, smooth coat sheds lightly and needs only a weekly wipe or brush, and at 12 to 25 pounds it is sturdy enough for rough-and-tumble play with older children. Bostons are easy to train, friendly with cats and other dogs, and need about 30 to 45 minutes of exercise a day. Barking is moderate; some will alert at the door but most settle quickly. The short muzzle is the main drawback: Bostons snore, overheat in hot weather and can have breathing and eye problems, so walks move to cooler hours in summer and a harness is kinder than a collar. Their prominent eyes can be scratched during play, so watch for squinting or redness.
picks.best_for: First-time owners wanting a playful, low-grooming small dog
picks.quirky_fact: The Boston Terrier was one of the first breeds developed in the United States, in the late 1800s.
picks.skip_if: You live somewhere hot without air conditioning or want a jogging dog

picks.description: The Maltese is a gentle toy dog that usually weighs under 7 pounds, with low energy and an easy-to-train nature. Short walks and indoor games cover its exercise needs, which makes it one of the easiest dogs here for people with limited mobility or time for long walks. It is rated good with children, cats and other dogs, though its small size means toddlers need close supervision. The long white coat has no undercoat and sheds little, but it needs daily brushing or a short clip every four to six weeks, plus regular cleaning around the eyes to prevent tear staining. Barking is moderate, and the breed can become vocal if left alone for long periods, which it dislikes. House-training a toy breed can take patience.
picks.best_for: Calm adults wanting a tiny, affectionate dog with little shedding
picks.quirky_fact: The Maltese has been kept as a companion dog for well over two thousand years around the Mediterranean.
picks.skip_if: You have toddlers or will not keep up with daily grooming

picks.description: The Miniature Schnauzer is the sturdiest dog in the top five, weighing 11 to 20 pounds, with a wiry coat that sheds very little. It is easy to train, gets along with children, cats and other dogs, and needs around 45 minutes of walks and play each day. Minis are alert and will announce visitors, so the barking is moderate rather than low; teaching a quiet cue early makes a real difference. The coat needs weekly brushing, with the beard and leg furnishings combed more often, and clipping or hand-stripping every six to eight weeks. The breed is prone to weight gain and pancreatitis on rich diets, so measured meals and few fatty treats help. Lifespan is 12 to 15 years.
picks.best_for: Active households wanting a sturdy, low-shedding small watchdog
picks.quirky_fact: Miniature Schnauzers were bred in Germany as farm ratters, which explains their alert, busy nature.
picks.skip_if: You share thin walls with neighbors and cannot train a quiet cue

picks.description: The Shih Tzu is the most relaxed dog in this list: low energy, happy with 20 to 30 minutes of gentle walking a day, and content to spend long stretches on the sofa. It is affectionate, friendly with children, cats and other dogs, and rarely needs much space. The trade-offs are coat care and stubbornness. The long coat sheds little but tangles quickly, so it needs daily brushing or a short puppy clip every four to six weeks, and the hair above the eyes is often tied up or trimmed. House-training can take longer than with eager-to-please breeds, and barking is moderate. The short muzzle makes it sensitive to heat, so summer walks belong in early morning or evening.
picks.best_for: Less active owners wanting a calm, cuddly indoor companion
picks.quirky_fact: Shih Tzu translates roughly as 'little lion', a nod to their status in the Chinese imperial court.
picks.skip_if: You want a quick learner or live somewhere hot without air conditioning

picks.description: The Papillon is a small dog with a working dog's brain. At 5 to 10 pounds it is easy to carry, but its energy is high and it is one of the easiest toy breeds to train, so it thrives on daily walks, fetch, and short training or agility sessions. It is friendly with children, cats and other dogs, though its fine bones mean rough play with young children is risky. The single silky coat sheds little and needs brushing once or twice a week, with no clipping required. Barking is moderate; Papillons are alert and will flag noises outside. A Papillon that gets too little activity can become restless and vocal, so it suits owners who want to do things with their dog rather than just cuddle it.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting a tiny dog for tricks, walks and dog sports
picks.quirky_fact: Papillon means 'butterfly' in French, named for the breed's large, fringed upright ears.
picks.skip_if: You want a low-energy lap dog or have rough young children

picks.description: The Miniature Poodle stands 10 to 15 inches tall and weighs roughly 10 to 15 pounds, combining a low-shedding coat with high intelligence and easy training. It is friendly with children, cats and other dogs and does well in family homes. Energy is high: plan on 45 to 60 minutes of walks and play a day, plus training games, or a bored Mini Poodle will invent its own entertainment. The curly coat sheds very little but never stops growing, so it needs brushing several times a week and a professional clip every four to six weeks. Barking is moderate, and Poodles are sensitive to tone, so harsh correction backfires. Lifespan is 12 to 15 years.
picks.best_for: Active families wanting a clever, low-shedding small dog
picks.quirky_fact: The traditional poodle show clip began as a practical cut that kept joints warm for water-retrieving dogs.
picks.skip_if: You cannot pay for regular grooming or give daily exercise

picks.description: The French Bulldog is rated low for barking and gets along with children, cats and other dogs, which makes it one of the easiest small dogs to keep near neighbors. It needs only 30 to 45 minutes of moderate exercise a day and its short coat needs little grooming beyond a weekly brush and cleaning the facial folds. It sits at the top of this weight range: many Frenchies stay under 25 pounds, but some males reach 28. The real cost is health. The flat face causes snoring and poor heat tolerance, and the breed is prone to breathing, spine and skin problems, so vet bills and insurance tend to be higher than average. Training is moderate, as Frenchies can be stubborn.
picks.best_for: Quiet homes wanting a playful, low-barking, low-grooming dog
picks.quirky_fact: Most French Bulldogs cannot swim well because of their heavy front ends, so pools and lakes need supervision.
picks.skip_if: You cannot afford higher vet costs or live somewhere hot

picks.description: The Westie is a friendly, confident terrier of 15 to 20 pounds that is rated good with children, cats and other dogs, which is less common among terriers. It needs about 45 minutes of daily activity and enjoys digging and sniffing games. Barking is moderate, and like most terriers it has an independent streak, so training takes consistency rather than force. The double, rough coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a couple of times a week, with hand-stripping or clipping every couple of months to keep it neat. Westies are prone to skin allergies, so itching and redness are worth watching. They tolerate cold well thanks to the coat and live 12 to 16 years.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a sturdy, playful terrier that tolerates other pets
picks.quirky_fact: Westies were bred white so hunters in Scotland could tell them apart from foxes in the field.
picks.skip_if: You want an off-leash dog or a garden free of dug holes

picks.description: The Pomeranian packs a big double coat and a bold personality into 3 to 7 pounds. It is friendly with children, cats and other dogs, has moderate energy that indoor play and short walks can cover, and it is intelligent enough to learn tricks quickly once motivated. The drawbacks are noise and fur: Poms are rated high for barking, alerting at every sound, and the dense coat sheds heavily and needs brushing several times a week, with seasonal blowouts. Their small size makes them fragile around young children and large dogs. Training is moderate, as they can be stubborn about house-training. A Pom suits someone who is home often and does not mind a vocal dog.
picks.best_for: Adults home often who want a tiny, bold and showy companion
picks.quirky_fact: Early Pomeranians were much larger sled-type dogs; Queen Victoria helped popularize the smaller size.
picks.skip_if: You need a quiet dog or dislike fur on furniture

picks.description: The Chihuahua is the smallest breed here, usually 2 to 6 pounds, and can live 12 to 20 years. It is loyal to its person, needs little space, and its short or long coat sheds lightly with simple grooming. Energy is moderate, covered by short walks and indoor play. It ranks lower for two reasons in the data: barking is rated high, and it is not rated as good with children. Chihuahuas often bond with one person and can be wary or snappy with strangers and grabby hands, and their fragile bodies are easily hurt. They get along with cats and other dogs when socialized. Training is moderate; house-training in cold or wet weather can be slow, and they need a sweater in winter.
picks.best_for: Single adults or couples wanting a long-lived, devoted tiny dog
picks.quirky_fact: The Chihuahua is named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua, where the breed was found in the 1800s.
picks.skip_if: You have young children or need a quiet dog for shared walls

picks.description: The Scottish Terrier is a dignified, independent terrier of 18 to 22 pounds that is loyal to its family and good with children who respect its space. It is not rated as good with cats or other dogs, which is why it sits lower here: its hunting instincts and tendency to stand its ground can cause trouble in multi-pet homes. Exercise needs are moderate, about 30 to 45 minutes a day. The wiry, dense coat sheds moderately and needs brushing weekly and stripping or clipping every couple of months. Barking is moderate, and Scotties are watchful, reserved with strangers, and stubborn to train, so they suit experienced owners who use patient, consistent methods.
picks.best_for: Single-pet homes wanting a loyal, independent terrier
picks.quirky_fact: A Scottish Terrier named Fala was one of the best-known White House pets during the Franklin Roosevelt years.
picks.skip_if: You have cats or other dogs, or want an eager-to-please dog

picks.description: The Miniature Pinscher is a fearless, high-energy dog of 8 to 10 pounds with a short coat that needs almost no grooming. It is rated good with children, cats and other dogs, but it is one of the harder small breeds to train and is rated high for barking. Min Pins need around an hour of activity a day and are known escape artists, slipping through gaps in fences and doors, so a secure yard and a reliable recall routine matter for their safety. Their short coat gives little protection from cold, so a coat or sweater helps in winter. They suit experienced owners who enjoy a busy, bold little dog and can handle its stubborn streak.
picks.best_for: Experienced, active owners wanting a bold, low-grooming small dog
picks.quirky_fact: Despite the name, the Miniature Pinscher is not a small Doberman; it is an older German breed.
picks.skip_if: You want an easy first dog or need low barking

picks.description: The Jack Russell Terrier is a working terrier of 13 to 17 pounds with the energy of a much larger dog. It needs an hour or more of vigorous exercise and mental work every day, and without it tends to bark, dig and chew. The coat is short, smooth, broken or rough, sheds lightly and needs only weekly brushing. Jack Russells are good with children and usually with other dogs, but they are not rated as good with cats, and their strong prey drive makes small pets risky. They are rated hard to train and high for barking, so they reward experienced owners who like an athletic, clever dog for long walks, ball games or earthdog sports rather than people seeking a calm small companion.
picks.best_for: Very active owners wanting a tireless partner for outdoor activity
picks.quirky_fact: The breed is named after Reverend John Russell, a 19th-century English clergyman who bred terriers for fox hunting.
picks.skip_if: You have cats or small pets, or want a calm house dog

faqs.question: What is the easiest small dog breed to own?
faqs.answer: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and the Havanese are among the easiest small dogs to live with. Both are easy to train, get along with children, cats and other dogs, and are rated low or moderate for barking. The trade-off is that both want company and do poorly when left alone for long workdays, and the Havanese coat needs regular brushing.

faqs.question: Which small dogs bark the least?
faqs.answer: In this list, the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and the French Bulldog are rated low for barking. The Chihuahua, Pomeranian, Miniature Pinscher and Jack Russell Terrier are rated high, so they suit detached homes better than buildings with shared walls. Any breed can become a nuisance barker if it is bored or left alone too long, so exercise and a taught quiet cue still matter.

faqs.question: Are small dogs good with young children?
faqs.answer: Many are, but size brings risks. Very small breeds like the Chihuahua, Papillon and Maltese can be injured if dropped or stepped on, and the Chihuahua is not rated as good with children. Sturdier small breeds such as the Boston Terrier, Havanese, Cavalier and Miniature Schnauzer usually cope better with family life. Supervise young children with any dog.

faqs.question: Which small dogs shed the least?
faqs.answer: The Maltese, Havanese, Shih Tzu, Miniature Poodle, and Miniature Schnauzer shed little. Low shedding usually means more grooming, though: these coats keep growing and need frequent brushing plus clipping every few weeks. No breed is free of allergens, so anyone with allergies should spend time with the breed before committing.

faqs.question: Do small dogs need less exercise than big dogs?
faqs.answer: Not always. The Shih Tzu and Maltese are content with short daily walks, but the Jack Russell Terrier, Miniature Pinscher, Papillon and Miniature Poodle are high-energy dogs that need an hour or more of activity and mental work each day. Choose by energy level, not by weight, if you have limited time for walks.

seo_title: Best Small Dog Breeds Under 25 Pounds (2026)
answer: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, Havanese and Boston Terrier are the best small dogs here: easy to train, good with children and other pets, and not prone to nuisance barking. Among small breeds, temperament and barking separate a pleasant dog from a difficult one far more than a few pounds of size.
method: We filtered a 150-breed dataset for toy and small breeds, then ordered them by trainability, barking level and how well each gets along with children, cats and other dogs, putting the easiest all-round companions first.
author: Elena Marsh
